chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Hamzah ibn Ya'la from Ali ibn Idris from Muhammad from his brother Abu Jarir from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said:
"Indeed, when a man is in prayer and his father calls him, he should say 'Subhanallah' (glorify God); and if his mother calls him, he should say 'Labbayk' (I am responding to you)."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: Prayer (specifically the ritual act of salat)
key_terms.لَبَّيْكِ: I am responding to you / At your service

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim respond to their parents' call while performing prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on forgetfulness (*sahw*), this hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) establishes a nuanced hierarchy of filial piety during prayer, prioritizing the father’s call with a concise *tasbih* to minimize disruption, while granting the mother a more responsive *labbayk*. This distinction reflects the Shia jurisprudential understanding of the mother’s elevated status and the practical need to balance the sanctity of *salat* with the immediate duty of honoring parents. It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining spiritual focus while fulfilling social obligations, illustrating the integration of ritual purity with familial respect.
